drivingQuestion: Does R. Yehuda's requirement to cut the veins apply to an animal as well, or only to a bird?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic gloss confining a tannaitic ruling to the case of a bird; nothing is challenged or resolved here.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בְּעוֹף, הוֹאִיל וְצוֹלֵהוּ כּוּלּוֹ כְּאֶחָד, אֲבָל בְּהֵמָה, כֵּיוָן דִּמְנַתְּחַהּ אֵבֶר אֵבֶר – לָא צְרִיךְ.
segments.en: § The mishna states: «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The slaughter is not valid «until he cuts» the veins in the neck. «Rav Ḥisda said: Rav Yehuda said» that one must cut the veins «only» in the slaughter of «a bird, as» one typically «roasts it in its entirety as one» whole entity; therefore, one must cut the veins to ensure that the blood drains. «But» with regard to the slaughter of «an animal, since it is» typically «quartered» into «limbs,» resulting in the blood draining more readily, one «need not» cut the veins.

moves.summary: quotes R. Yehuda's clause from the mishna
moves.about: R. Yehuda's clause in the mishna requiring that the veins be cut

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: לא אמר רבי יהודה אלא בעוף
moves.summary: confines R. Yehuda's requirement to a bird, because a bird is roasted whole
moves.about: R. Yehuda required cutting the veins only for a bird, not for an animal

moves.cueHe: אבל בהמה, כיון דמנתחה אבר אבר
moves.summary: an animal is quartered limb by limb, so its veins need not be cut
moves.about: the reason for the limitation — a bird is roasted whole, so the blood must be drained by cutting the veins, whereas an animal is quartered
